A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReLIFT study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support matching retained, relocated, revised, and newly added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original RL/SFT training-dynamics experiments, ReLIFT benchmark evaluations, scheduling/data-selection ablations, and experiments with additional Qwen models.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations and ablations, including additional hybrid baselines, Llama experiments, resource measurements, entropy sensitivity, and reasoning-behavior analyses.

M1.justification: V1 uses plain cross-entropy for interleaved fine-tuning. V2 adds token-distribution entropy regularization in Equation (4), with alpha set to 0.0001. This changes the fine-tuning objective, while retaining the hardest-question selection, verified-demonstration buffer, GRPO training, and adaptive interleaving procedure.

E1.justification: Both use OpenR1/NuminaMath-derived mathematical training data and evaluate AIME 2024, AIME 2025, AMC, MATH500, OlympiadBench, and MMLU-Pro. V2's Llama experiments and differently filtered subsets change model configurations and protocols within this retained coverage. Its new behavioral analyses use existing AIME25 tasks.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds RL w/ SFT loss and two SFT then RL variants, including a demonstration-matched sequential control. The original pure SFT/RL, LUFFY, and four prior RLVR comparators remain. These additions substantially expand the comparison against alternative ways of combining SFT and RL.

E3.justification: The reported main training subset changes from 45k to 46k examples, with correctness/length filtering specified in v2. The Qwen2.5-Math-7B budget changes from 500 to 600 steps, and SFT batch size/learning rate from 128/1e-5 to 64/5e-5. V2 adds sequential-training controls, Llama settings using 11k short solutions and a 2048-token cap, and GPU-hour and normalized-keyword measurements.

E4.justification: V2 retains the all/uniform/random ablations, moving their detailed table to Appendix D. It adds an entropy-coefficient sensitivity study, AIME25 keyword-frequency analysis, and a worked case comparing completeness and verbosity across methods. The hardest-question-count trajectory previously shown in Figure 3c is removed.

E5.justification: The avg@32 reporting for the small competition test sets is retained. Neither version specifies repeated training runs or seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance procedures. V2's additional plots do not introduce an uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main ReLIFT overall accuracy/length changes from 51.1/1061 in v1 Table 1 to 52.6/3502 in v2 Table 1, alongside changed training conditions. Many baseline and model entries also change. Scheduling-ablation accuracies are retained but their lengths are revised. Hybrid, Llama, resource, coefficient-sweep, and behavioral results are added; these are not isolated same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 adds the mathematical definition of the entropy-regularized fine-tuning objective and its weighting parameter in Equation (4). The GRPO objective, hardest-example buffer definition, and cross-entropy formulation remain substantively unchanged. No theorem or proof development is added.

C1.justification: The central claims about RL/SFT complementarity and selective interleaving remain. V2 expands its headline comparison to joint-loss and sequential hybrid methods and adds a claim of reduced training time. V1's specific 13% demonstration and nearly tenfold response-length framing gives way to broader data and computational-efficiency claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains entropy regularization as protecting exploration during fine-tuning. Appendix E interprets keyword frequencies as evidence of confidence and stronger planning. Appendices B–C add concrete Llama limitations: the full training set is too challenging and the Qwen prompt cannot be followed. The original interpretation of adaptive hardest-question training largely remains.

D1.justification: V2 adds filtering instructions, the SFT hyperparameter-search grid and LLaMA-Factory implementation, hybrid-loss construction, sequential-training details, Llama-specific instructions, and per-method GPU costs. Reported hardware changes from 16 to 8 A800 GPUs. Conversely, v1's explicit RoPE/context-extension settings, RL entropy coefficient, and VERL disclosure disappear; omission does not establish that those settings changed. The repository link target is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds discussion and citations concerning entropy-limited exploration, online difficulty filtering, and DAPO, alongside newer model and implementation references. It elaborates the cited arguments about RL's capability limits, while retaining the central positioning of ReLIFT relative to sequential SFT/RL and LUFFY.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and results narrative are extensively revised, with an explicit contribution list added. Experimental setup and results become separate sections, much implementation material moves into Appendix B, and the original appendix is reorganized into several thematic appendices.

P2.justification: V2 redraws Figure 1, reorganizes the main tables into method/model groups, and changes Figure 3 from four panels to three. The detailed ablation table moves to Appendix D and gains a main-text bar-chart summary. New displays include the resource table, entropy sweep, Llama prompt, keyword plots, and boxed case-study responses.

improvement.justification: The new joint-loss and sequential SFT/RL controls, including a demonstration-matched variant, address a major gap in v1's evidence for adaptive interleaving. The entropy ablation and measured GPU costs further strengthen that central comparison. These gains outweigh omitted earlier implementation settings and remaining overstatements: Table 1 does not support universal top-two rankings, and Table 2 limits training-time savings to hybrid baselines.
